title: Not whether inherent grace exists, but how to read those texts; locus closed
source_text: XLIX. Ac proinde non quaeritur simpliciter, An Detur aliqua gratia salvifica nobis inhaerens per modum sive actus, sive habitus: sed istud tantum An de ejusmodi gratia intelligenda sint ea scripturae loca ubi salus nostra & justificatio gratiae Dei tribuitur, quod affirmant Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae, Reformati vero negant. Quae quaestio quanti sit momenti, alibi fusius a nobis expensum est.
pass_a_gloss: XLIX. And accordingly it is not asked simply, Whether there is given some saving grace inhering in us by way either of act, or of habit: but this only Whether of grace of this kind are to be understood those places of scripture where our salvation and justification is attributed to the grace of God, which the Doctors of the Roman Church affirm, but the Reformed deny. Of how great moment this question is, has been weighed more fully by us elsewhere.
pass_b_english: Thesis XLIX. So the question is not simply whether there is a saving grace that inheres in us, either as an act or as a habit. It is only whether the passages of scripture that ascribe our salvation and justification to God's grace are to be understood of such grace.
The doctors of the Roman Church say yes and the Reformed say no. How much this question matters we have considered more fully elsewhere.
